programme: NCOR2 and HDAC3 constitute the canonical NCoR/SMRT-HDAC3 nuclear-receptor corepressor complex (NCOR2 recruits and activates HDAC3 as its deacetylase partner); among their concordant target sets, NCOR2 reaches TH (tyrosine hydroxylase, the rate-limiting catecholamine-synthesis enzyme) and the nuclear receptors AR, RARA, PPARD, NR2F2 and NR1I2, while HDAC3 reaches GATA2, the transcription factor that switches on TH/DBH in the sympathoadrenal/chromaffin lineage. ETV1, an ETS-family factor with a documented ETS site in the TH promoter, independently targets TH and AR. Together the three converge on a single node: transcriptional control of catecholamine biosynthesis and adrenergic/nuclear-receptor tone.
role_in_a: In cardiovascular tissue this corepressor/ETS node would set the transcriptional ceiling on adrenergic and nuclear-receptor-driven gene programmes (AR, RARA, PPARD, NR2F2) that govern vascular tone, cardiac remodeling and the response to catecholamine load — the same axis implicated in hypertensive and catecholamine-associated cardiovascular disease (stress cardiomyopathy, arrhythmia, vascular remodeling).
role_in_b: In chromaffin/paraganglion cells this is the biosynthetic control point itself: GATA2-driven activation of TH, reinforced by ETV1 and tempered by NCOR2/AR-pathway repression, sets catecholamine output — the defining biochemical lesion of pheochromocytoma and paraganglioma and the basis of its diagnostic test (elevated catecholamines/metanephrines).
shared_axis: PPGL tumors overproduce catecholamines through a GATA2/TH-driven programme, and that catecholamine excess is a direct, clinically established cause of cardiovascular pathology (hypertension, catecholamine cardiomyopathy, arrhythmia). A corepressor/ETS module that sets TH and nuclear-receptor tone would therefore be expected to recur as a concordant regulon in networks built from both adrenal (tumor) and blood (cardiovascular) patient groups, without needing a paper that states the two diseases together.
reasoning: The module is nameable from core, undisputed molecular biology (NCoR2-HDAC3 complex; ETS regulation of the TH promoter; GATA2 as the chromaffin TH/DBH switch), and catecholamine excess causing cardiovascular disease in PPGL is textbook clinical fact, so the connection follows without being invented. But the record itself is essentially empty for these specific factors — zero Open Targets associations across all 12 factors for either disease, and the only two papers retrieved (for ETV1 and NCOR2) are respectively unclear and off-topic — so the account rests on domain reasoning, not on anything the retrieval surfaced.
support: none found — the only two papers retrieved in this record (PMID 20534969, retrieved for ETV1 against disease B, abstract truncated, unclear whether ETV1 is actually discussed; PMID 22017809, retrieved for NCOR2 against disease B, but its title/abstract concern spermatogenesis, not PPGL or cardiovascular disease) cannot be used as support.
how_to_falsify: Knock down NCOR2, HDAC3, and ETV1 individually and in combination in a chromaffin-lineage PPGL model (e.g., PC12 cells or primary human PPGL culture) and measure TH transcription, GATA2 expression, and catecholamine/metanephrine output; in parallel, ChIP for NCOR2/HDAC3/ETV1 occupancy at the TH and GATA2 loci in chromaffin cells versus vascular/cardiac tissue. If TH transcription and catecholamine output are unaffected by loss of these factors, or if none of the three occupy the TH/GATA2 loci in either tissue, the proposed shared node is wrong.
caveats: Tissue pairing is adrenal (tumor) versus blood (circulating/surrogate for cardiovascular disease), so the cardiac/adrenergic claim rests on catecholamine physiology rather than on matched vascular or myocardial tissue expression. The 80 patient-group comparisons are drawn from only 4 independent cohort pairs, so counts like 39/80 and 34/80 reflect repeated slicing of a small number of underlying cohorts, not 80 independent replications. FOSB also targets TH but is marked discordant here and was deliberately excluded — its divergence between the two diseases should not be read as reinforcing this module. Nine of the twelve concordant factors (ZNF24, RFX1, LBX1, MECP2, LMX1B, SALL4, PURB, MAML2, and discordant FOSB) point toward other, non-overlapping candidate programmes (MHC-II/antigen presentation via RFX1, cardiac-muscle/neuronal genes via MECP2, EMT via LBX1, stemness via SALL4, podocyte/developmental genes via LMX1B, Notch via MAML2) — this account covers only the TH/GATA2/AR-converging subset and does not claim the full factor set acts as one module.
